correctness.rationale: The proof handles the exact floor/remainder exponent, all degrees and endpoints, and the \(M=1\) degenerate case. At any interior non-breakpoint all floor quotients persist, so the objective strictly decreases. The candidate-count bound follows from the standard two-range bound for distinct floor quotients. The supplied checker independently confirms the theorem for 16,275 exponent vectors with entries at most 25 and replays the Reyssat case; finite testing is not used as the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem directly sharpens an explicit finite optimization posed in recent abc-triple work: it replaces a scan of \(M-1\) degrees by an exact union of quotient breakpoints of size at most twice the sum of square roots of the valuations. This is a reusable algorithmic lemma for large prime-power exponents and gives a structural explanation of which degree regimes matter in the canonical Reyssat example.
